words.meaning: A strong feeling of love and pride for one's country.

medium.simple_explanation: A strong feeling of pride and love for your own country, often wanting it to be independent.
medium.funny_explanation: It's like being the ultimate fan-girl or fan-boy for your country, wearing its colors and cheering for it like it's the only team that matters in the world cup of history.

examples.text: Nationalism inspired people to fight for their country's freedom.
My nationalism is so high that I think our local street food should be on the national flag.

words.meaning: Relating to the present time or recent history.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to the present or recent times, rather than the distant past.
medium.funny_explanation: Anything that doesn't involve using a carrier pigeon to send a meme or wearing a powdered wig to school.

examples.text: Modern technology has changed how we learn about history.
My grandma thinks using a microwave is peak modern living, but I'm waiting for hoverboards.

words.meaning: Connected with something else in some way.
The act of creating or starting something new.

medium.simple_explanation: The act of creating or developing something over time.
medium.funny_explanation: Like watching a messy pile of LEGOs slowly become a Death Star, but with countries and laws instead of plastic bricks.

examples.text: The formation of the new club took several weeks of planning.
The formation of my science project usually happens five minutes before the bus arrives.

words.meaning: Countries where people share a common culture and government.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To define the modern political unit that replaced old empires in Europe and changed how people identified themselves.
hard.simple_explanation: Countries where the citizens share a common language, culture, and history.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a giant club where everyone wears the same jersey, sings the same anthem, and follows the same rules, rather than just living in whatever backyard a King says is his.

examples.text: The rise of nationalism led to the formation of many new nation-states in Europe.
Living in a nation-state is like a permanent school spirit week where everyone actually likes the mascot.

hard.real_world_analogy: A nation-state is like a family home where everyone agrees on the house rules, as opposed to a hotel where random strangers just happen to be in the same building.

words.meaning: Who a person is or what they represent.

medium.simple_explanation: The qualities and beliefs that make a person or group who they are.
medium.funny_explanation: It’s your personal 'brand'—like how your identity might be 'the kid who always has snacks' or 'the person who sleeps through math'.

examples.text: Music and language are important parts of a nation's identity.
My cat has a secret identity as a midnight ninja who knocks over water glasses.

words.meaning: A feeling or awareness about something.
Feeling like an accepted member of a group.
Signs or objects that represent an idea.
Important pictures or signs used to represent something.

medium.simple_explanation: Symbols or people that represent important ideas or movements.
medium.funny_explanation: Not the little pictures on your phone screen, but real-life superstars of history that people look up to like heroes.

examples.text: The spinning wheel became one of the famous icons of the Indian freedom struggle.
In this house, the refrigerator is one of the most respected icons because it holds the pizza.

words.meaning: Created something strong with a lot of effort.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe how new identities and links between people were created through hard work and shared struggle.
hard.simple_explanation: Created or shaped through great effort and heat (like metal).
hard.funny_explanation: It's like making a giant friendship bracelet, but instead of string, you're using heavy iron and a very hot furnace to make sure it never breaks.

examples.text: The common struggle against the British forged a strong bond between different Indian communities.
Their friendship was forged in the cafeteria line during the great 'No-Pizza' crisis of 2023.

hard.real_world_analogy: A blacksmith hitting a glowing piece of iron to make a sword; the identity of the nation was 'hammered' into shape by history.

words.meaning: Gave a new meaning or description to something.

medium.simple_explanation: To give a new meaning to something or change how it is understood.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you tell your parents 'cleaning' now means 'shoving everything under the bed'—you just redefined the word!

examples.text: The new laws redefined what it meant to be a citizen.
I redefined my diet to include chocolate as a primary vegetable.

words.meaning: Lines that mark the limits of an area.

medium.simple_explanation: The limits or edges of an area, or the rules about what is allowed.
medium.funny_explanation: The invisible 'do not cross' line between you and your sibling in the back seat of a car.

examples.text: The explorers crossed the boundaries of the unknown territory.
My dog doesn't understand the boundaries of my personal space when I'm eating a burger.

words.meaning: Groups of people living or working together.
A series of actions taken to achieve something.

medium.simple_explanation: A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular result.
medium.funny_explanation: The agonizingly slow series of events that starts with 'I'll just check TikTok' and ends two hours later with you knowing how to make a tiny clay frog.

examples.text: Learning a new language is a long and difficult process.
The process of getting out of bed on a Monday requires at least three alarms and a miracle.

words.meaning: Being aware of something within a group.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To explain the awakening of a collective awareness among Indians about their national identity.
hard.simple_explanation: The state of being aware of something or a shared sense of identity.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like that 'Aha!' moment when the whole class realizes the teacher forgot to assign homework, and everyone stays quiet together.

examples.text: A new national consciousness began to emerge as people realized they shared a common enemy.
My cat has no consciousness of the fact that the 3 AM 'zoomies' wake the entire neighborhood.

hard.real_world_analogy: Consciousness is like a light bulb suddenly turning on in a dark room, letting everyone see that they are all standing in the same place.

words.meaning: To come out or become known.
A country located in Southeast Asia.
Lands controlled by a more powerful foreign country.

medium.simple_explanation: Countries or areas under the full or partial political control of another country.
medium.funny_explanation: Imagine a bully taking over your treehouse, making the rules, and eating your snacks—that’s basically what a powerful country does to its colonies.

examples.text: Many African and Asian countries were once colonies of European powers.
I tried to turn the living room into one of my private colonies, but the Queen (my mom) shut it down.

words.meaning: In a very close and personal way.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To show the deep and inseparable connection between nationalism and the fight against the British.
hard.simple_explanation: In a very close or personal way.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of how closely your teeth are connected to your braces—you can't really talk about one without the other!

examples.text: The growth of nationalism was intimately connected to the anti-colonial movement.
My dog is intimately connected to my sandwich; wherever the sandwich goes, the dog is two inches away.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like two best friends who share every secret; you can't understand one's history without knowing the other.

words.meaning: Being against the rule of a foreign country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the specific type of movement in India that fought against foreign rule.
hard.simple_explanation: Opposed to the system where one country rules over another.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like telling an uninvited guest who has moved into your bedroom and started eating your snacks that it's time for them to pack up and leave.

examples.text: Many countries in Asia and Africa led anti-colonial movements to gain independence.
I started an anti-colonial movement in my room when my little brother tried to claim the top bunk as his territory.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a security system that activates when someone tries to enter a house they don't own.

words.meaning: The state of being joined together as one.
A long and difficult fight for something.
Control by one country over another country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To name the system of foreign rule that India was struggling against.
hard.simple_explanation: When a powerful country takes control of another territory and its people.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a neighbor coming over, taking your TV, telling you what time to eat, and making you pay them for the privilege of living in your own house.

examples.text: Colonialism led to the exploitation of India's resources by the British Empire.
The cat's version of colonialism involves sitting on my laptop until I acknowledge it as the true king of the desk.

hard.real_world_analogy: A parasite that moves into a host body and starts taking all the nutrients for itself while trying to run the whole show.

words.meaning: Treated cruelly or unfairly by those in power.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the harsh and unfair treatment people faced under British rule, which united them.
hard.simple_explanation: Subject to harsh and authoritarian treatment.
hard.funny_explanation: It’s like being forced to wear a very heavy, itchy sweater in the middle of summer and not being allowed to complain about it.

examples.text: The oppressed people eventually rose up to demand their basic rights.
I felt truly oppressed when my mom made me eat broccoli before I could have the chocolate cake.

hard.real_world_analogy: Imagine a giant foot trying to keep a small spring pushed down; eventually, the spring is going to push back.

words.meaning: Used or felt by many people together.
A strong connection between people or groups.
A group based on social or economic status.
Things that have happened to someone.

medium.simple_explanation: Things that have happened to you and how they affected you.
medium.funny_explanation: A collection of all your 'oops' moments, 'yay' moments, and 'why did I eat that?' moments.

examples.text: Travel provides people with many interesting experiences.
My experiences with home-made haircuts usually end with me wearing a hat for a month.

words.meaning: Including many different types or kinds.

medium.simple_explanation: Involving many different types of things or people.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a 'choose your own adventure' book where every page leads to a different weird ending.

examples.text: The students in the class have varied interests, from sports to coding.
The reasons why I forgot my homework are varied and creative, ranging from aliens to a very hungry dog.

words.meaning: Ideas or beliefs about something.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To show that different groups of people had different ideas about what 'freedom' actually meant.
hard.simple_explanation: Opinions, beliefs, or ideas about something.
hard.funny_explanation: The little thought-bubbles that float over people's heads when they are daydreaming about how things should be.

examples.text: Different social groups had varying notions of what freedom would look like for them.
My notion of a perfect weekend involves twelve hours of video games, but my dad has other ideas involving a lawnmower.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like different people looking at a cloud and one seeing a dragon while the other sees a marshmallow.

words.meaning: A large formal meeting or a political group.

medium.simple_explanation: A formal meeting or a group of people who represent others to make decisions.
medium.funny_explanation: A giant group chat, but in person, with more suits and way more arguing about rules.

examples.text: The Indian National Congress played a key role in the freedom movement.
We held a family congress to decide if we should get a dog or a lizard.

words.meaning: A serious disagreement or fight.
A period of ten years.

medium.simple_explanation: A period of ten years.
medium.funny_explanation: Long enough for you to go from a toddler in diapers to a middle-schooler who thinks they're too cool for diapers.

examples.text: The world has changed significantly in the last decade.
It feels like it’s been a decade since lunch, but my watch says it's only been ten minutes.

words.meaning: The number twenty in a series.
One of the main parts of a book.
Refusing to help or work with the government.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To introduce one of the main peaceful protest methods used by Gandhi.
hard.simple_explanation: The refusal to cooperate or work with a government or organization.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine your parents ask you to clean your room, and you don't scream or fight—you just stand perfectly still like a statue and do absolutely nothing.

examples.text: The Non-Cooperation Movement aimed to stall the British administration by refusing to use their services.
My dog practiced non-cooperation when he realized we were heading toward the vet instead of the park.

hard.real_world_analogy: A giant machine where everyone suddenly stops turning their gears; the machine can't work without the people's help.

words.meaning: Relating to ordinary citizens of a country.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to ordinary citizens and their concerns, rather than military or religious matters.
medium.funny_explanation: The 'polite' version of a fight—you're not using tanks, you're just using your rights as a person to say 'no thanks' to the government.

examples.text: The group fought for civil rights for all citizens.
I tried to maintain a civil tone while my brother ate the last donut, but I failed.

words.meaning: Refusal to follow rules or orders.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To introduce the Civil Disobedience Movement, where people deliberately broke unfair laws.
hard.simple_explanation: Refusing to obey rules or laws as a form of protest.
hard.funny_explanation: When the sign says 'Do Not Touch' and you very slowly and dramatically touch it with your pinky finger while looking at the guard.

examples.text: Civil disobedience was a powerful tool used to challenge the Salt Laws.
The toddler's act of disobedience involved eating the cookie while maintaining direct eye contact with her mother.

hard.real_world_analogy: Refusing to pay for a ticket to a movie that is already free, just to prove the ticket booth shouldn't be there.

words.meaning: To look into something closely to learn more.

medium.simple_explanation: To travel through or search an area to learn about it.
medium.funny_explanation: Like being a detective in your own neighborhood, or looking for that one missing sock in the 'dark abyss' under your bed.

examples.text: Scientists want to explore the surface of Mars.
I decided to explore the back of the pantry and found snacks from 2012.

words.meaning: Tried to find or achieve something.

medium.simple_explanation: The past tense of seek; tried to find or achieve something.
medium.funny_explanation: A fancy way of saying you looked for something—usually used for big goals, not just seeking the TV remote.

examples.text: The leaders sought a peaceful solution to the conflict.
I sought the perfect selfie for an hour before giving up and taking a nap.

words.meaning: Relating to society and the people in it.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to society or how people live and interact in groups.
medium.funny_explanation: Anything that involves other humans—basically the reason you have a phone and the reason you have to wear pants outside.

examples.text: Different social groups had different goals for the country.
My social battery is currently at 1%, please do not talk to me.

words.meaning: Took part in an activity or event.

medium.simple_explanation: Took part in an activity or event.
medium.funny_explanation: Actually doing the group project instead of just putting your name on the poster at the last second.

examples.text: Everyone in the village participated in the festival.
I participated in the race, if you count 'walking slowly while eating a snack' as racing.

words.meaning: Caught or took control of something.

medium.simple_explanation: To succeed in getting someone’s interest or affection; or to take control of something.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when a new video game trailer 'captures' your brain and you can't think about anything else for a week.

examples.text: The beautiful scenery captured the artist's attention.
The scent of bacon captured my attention and led me straight to the kitchen.

words.meaning: The ability to form new ideas in the mind.

medium.simple_explanation: The ability of the mind to be creative or to think of new ideas.
medium.funny_explanation: The magical brain-theater where you can fly, be a billionaire, or imagine a world where homework is illegal.

examples.text: It takes a lot of imagination to write a science fiction novel.
My imagination is great at coming up with reasons why there might be a monster in my closet.

words.meaning: Involving a very large number of people.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the huge scale and number of people involved in the national movement.
hard.simple_explanation: Involving a very large number of people.
hard.funny_explanation: Not just a few friends, but so many people that you couldn't even count their shoes if you tried.

examples.text: The leaders organized mass protests to show the strength of the movement.
There was a mass exodus toward the cafeteria when the 'Free Pizza' sign was posted.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a tidal wave made of people instead of water; it’s impossible to stop because there's just so much of it.

words.meaning: Groups of people moving forward in a formal line.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe the organized groups of people marching in the streets during protests.
hard.simple_explanation: A number of people moving forward in an orderly, often formal, way.
hard.funny_explanation: Like a parade, but instead of floats and candy, people are carrying flags and shouting for their rights.

examples.text: Mass processions on the streets were used to demonstrate unity against the British.
The ants had a tiny procession toward the dropped crumb on the kitchen floor.

hard.real_world_analogy: A line of dominoes that keeps moving forward, showing everyone the path they are taking together.

words.meaning: A typical or important part of something.

medium.simple_explanation: A typical or noticeable quality or part of something.
medium.funny_explanation: Like how a 'feature' of a teenager's room is usually a floor you can't actually see because of the laundry.

examples.text: Large windows are a common feature of modern houses.
The main feature of my cooking is that the smoke alarm always goes off.

words.meaning: Belonging to the same time period.

medium.simple_explanation: Belonging to the same time period or happening right now
medium.funny_explanation: It’s like being alive at the same time as your favorite YouTuber instead of living in the era of dinosaurs.

examples.text: The textbook covers India and the contemporary world history.
In a contemporary world, we don't send letters; we just spam emojis.

words.meaning: Group working for their country's freedom.

medium.simple_explanation: A big organized effort by people across a whole country to achieve a common goal, like freedom
medium.funny_explanation: Imagine the whole school joining together to demand a 2-hour lunch break—that's basically a school-wide movement!

examples.text: The national movement for independence spread to every corner of India.
The national movement against homework was unfortunately cancelled by the teachers.

words.meaning: Reaching out to more people or areas.
Including something as part of a group.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this to show how the national movement was expanding and including many different types of people.
hard.simple_explanation: Including or absorbing something as part of a whole.
hard.funny_explanation: Like inviting every single pizza topping you can find onto one giant crust so everyone gets a bite.

examples.text: The national movement was incorporating new social groups after 1919.
I am incorporating chocolate chips, gummy bears, and sprinkles into my morning cereal.

hard.real_world_analogy: A snowball rolling down a hill and picking up leaves, sticks, and smaller snowballs to become one giant ball.

words.meaning: Categories of people in a society.

medium.simple_explanation: Collections of people who share the same background, job, or identity
medium.funny_explanation: In your school, the 'gamers' and the 'theater kids' are basically different social groups.

examples.text: New social groups like industrial workers joined the struggle for freedom.
My social group consists mostly of people who forget their lunch money every day.

words.meaning: Specific ways of doing things.

medium.simple_explanation: Different ways or methods of doing something
medium.funny_explanation: Just like your phone has 'Silent Mode' and 'Vibrate Mode,' the leaders had different modes of struggle.

examples.text: Mahatma Gandhi suggested new modes of struggle against British rule.
I have two modes during the weekend: 'Sleep' and 'Eat everything in the fridge'.

words.meaning: A long and difficult effort.
New events or changes in a situation.

medium.simple_explanation: New events or changes that happen over time
medium.funny_explanation: The sudden development of a giant pimple on my nose right before the party was not part of the plan.

examples.text: Historians try to understand the political developments that led to the war.
Latest developments: I have finally learned how to tie my shoelaces in under ten seconds.

words.meaning: Possible effects or results of an action.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author asks this to make the reader think about the long-term consequences of the changes after the war.
hard.simple_explanation: The possible future effects or results of an action.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'uh-oh' moments or surprises that happen after you decide to do something, like giving a cat a bath.

examples.text: The changes in the economic situation had serious implications for common people.
The implications of eating five ghost peppers are usually felt by your stomach ten minutes later.

hard.real_world_analogy: Dropping a pebble in a pond; the ripples that spread out across the water are the implications.

words.meaning: Relating to money and trade.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to money, trade, and how resources are used
medium.funny_explanation: My current economic situation is basically me checking my pockets and finding only a candy wrapper.

examples.text: The war created a very difficult economic situation with high taxes.
I made an economic decision to buy chocolate instead of a notebook.

words.meaning: The state of government and power.

medium.simple_explanation: The current state of government power and laws
medium.funny_explanation: The political situation in the cafeteria got tense when they ran out of pizza.

examples.text: The political situation changed drastically after the First World War.
I tried to improve my political situation at home by offering to do the dishes.

words.meaning: Money spent by a person or government.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe the massive amount of money the British government spent on fighting the First World War.
hard.simple_explanation: An amount of money spent.
hard.funny_explanation: Your piggy bank’s worst nightmare—when money goes 'poof' and disappears into the shopkeeper's hand.

examples.text: The war led to a huge increase in defence expenditure.
My weekly expenditure on comic books is way higher than my expenditure on boring green vegetables.

hard.real_world_analogy: Water flowing out of a tank through a tap; the more you open the tap, the higher the expenditure.

words.meaning: Money borrowed to pay for a war.

medium.simple_explanation: Money borrowed by the government to pay for fighting a war
medium.funny_explanation: It's like asking your friend for money to buy a water balloon, but you have to pay them back double later.

examples.text: The British government financed the war using massive war loans.
I need a 'snack loan' from my brother to get through this afternoon.

words.meaning: Taxes on goods entering a country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To explain how the British raised money for the war by taxing goods entering the country.
hard.simple_explanation: Taxes paid on goods brought into or sent out of a country.
hard.funny_explanation: A 'toll booth' for packages that want to cross the border and go on vacation in a new country.

examples.text: Customs duties were raised to help finance the war loans.
Imagine if your mom charged you customs duties every time you brought a chocolate bar into your bedroom from the kitchen.

hard.real_world_analogy: An entry fee you have to pay at a fair just to be allowed to bring your own popcorn inside.

words.meaning: Tax paid on money earned by people.

medium.simple_explanation: A part of your earnings that you must pay to the government
medium.funny_explanation: Imagine your parents giving you 10 dollars for chores, but then taking 2 back just for 'using the house floor'.

examples.text: To pay for the war, the government introduced income tax for the first time.
If there was an income tax on my allowance, I’d be broke in five minutes.

words.meaning: To start something for the first time.
Very great or intense.

medium.simple_explanation: Very great or intense; far beyond the normal level
medium.funny_explanation: The level of laziness I feel on a rainy Sunday morning is absolutely extreme.

examples.text: High prices caused extreme hardship for common people.
My reaction to finding a spider in my shoe was extreme, involving a lot of screaming.

words.meaning: Suffering caused by lack of basic things.

medium.simple_explanation: A condition that is very difficult to endure; suffering
medium.funny_explanation: The hardship of having no Wi-Fi for an hour is a pain no middle-schooler should face.

examples.text: Millions of people faced extreme hardship during the war years.
Walking to the kitchen to get water is a major hardship when the movie is good.

words.meaning: To provide something that is needed.
Forcing people to join the army.

medium.simple_explanation: Making people join the army against their will
medium.funny_explanation: It's like being 'volunteered' by your mom to help clean the garage when you had plans to play video games.

examples.text: Forced recruitment in villages caused widespread anger against the British.
My sister's forced recruitment of me into her tea party was very annoying.

words.meaning: Places in the countryside.

medium.simple_explanation: Areas in the countryside, like villages and farms, away from the city
medium.funny_explanation: A place where there are more cows than streetlights and the nearest mall is a day's journey away.

examples.text: Forced recruitment was most common in the rural areas of India.
In rural areas, my phone's signal is basically non-existent.

words.meaning: Existing in many different places.

medium.simple_explanation: Found or happening over a large area or among many people
medium.funny_explanation: Like a rumor that starts in the first period and is known by the whole school by lunch.

examples.text: There was widespread anger among the people due to the food shortages.
There was widespread panic when the teacher said, 'Clear your desks for a quiz'.

words.meaning: Very severe or serious.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To emphasize how extremely severe the food shortages were for the Indian people.
hard.simple_explanation: Very serious, severe, or intense.
hard.funny_explanation: Not 'cute' like a puppy, but 'a-cute' like the sharp pain you feel when you stub your toe on a Lego.

examples.text: The crop failure resulted in acute shortages of food across the country.
I have an acute need for a nap after doing exactly three minutes of homework.

hard.real_world_analogy: The difference between a tiny water leak and a pipe bursting and flooding your whole house.

words.meaning: Having too little of something.

medium.simple_explanation: When there is not enough of something that is needed
medium.funny_explanation: There is a serious shortage of brain cells in my head when I look at a geometry problem.

examples.text: Crop failures led to acute shortages of food across the country.
The shortage of snacks in this house is a national emergency.

words.meaning: Happening at the same time as something.

medium.simple_explanation: Happening at the same time as something else or going along with it
medium.funny_explanation: Usually, my bad grades are accompanied by a long lecture from my parents.

examples.text: The food shortage was accompanied by a deadly influenza epidemic.
I am always accompanied by my dog, who thinks he's my bodyguard.

words.meaning: A serious illness caused by a virus.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To identify the specific deadly virus that spread throughout India after the war.
hard.simple_explanation: A highly contagious viral infection, commonly known as the flu.
hard.funny_explanation: An invisible army of tiny germs that turns your nose into a leaky faucet and makes your body feel like a wet noodle.

examples.text: The influenza epidemic caused millions of deaths in 1921.
Influenza turned my brother into a sneezing, tissue-wasting monster for a whole week.

hard.real_world_analogy: A computer virus, but instead of crashing your laptop, it makes your lungs and throat feel 'glitchy'.

words.meaning: A disease that spreads very fast.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe how the disease affected a huge number of people at the same time.
hard.simple_explanation: A widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a community.
hard.funny_explanation: When one person yawns and suddenly the whole classroom is doing it, but with itchy germs instead of yawns.

examples.text: The combination of famine and epidemic led to a massive loss of life.
There is currently an epidemic of silly faces whenever someone tries to take a serious group photo.

hard.real_world_analogy: A wildfire that jumps from tree to tree very quickly until the whole forest is involved.

words.meaning: An official count of the population.

medium.simple_explanation: An official count of all the people living in a country
medium.funny_explanation: It's the government's way of doing roll call for the whole nation to see who's actually home.

examples.text: According to the census of 1921, millions of people died due to famine.
If I ran a census of my room, I'd find 1 human and 47 empty soda cans.

words.meaning: Died, especially in a sudden way.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this formal word to describe the tragic and massive loss of life.
hard.simple_explanation: Died, especially in a violent, sudden, or untimely way.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like the ultimate 'Game Over' screen for millions of people at once in history's saddest level.

examples.text: According to the census, 12 to 13 million people perished in the famines.
My hopes of getting an extra scoop of ice cream perished when my dad saw the empty carton in the bin.

hard.real_world_analogy: A candle flame being snuffed out by a sudden, cold gust of wind.

words.meaning: Periods when there is no food.

medium.simple_explanation: Extreme lack of food that causes many people to go hungry
medium.funny_explanation: My stomach thinks there's a famine every single day right before the lunch bell rings.

examples.text: Famines and epidemics led to the deaths of millions in the early 1920s.
The Great Cookie Famine of 2023 happened when my brother found the hidden jar.

words.meaning: To come into view or arrive.
A non-violent method of protest.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Introduced as Gandhi's core philosophy and method for fighting injustice without violence.
hard.simple_explanation: A policy of non-violent political resistance based on the power of truth.
hard.funny_explanation: Fighting with 'Truth Power' instead of punching; basically the ultimate 'I’m not moving until you do what's right' move.

examples.text: Gandhiji successfully led the satyagraha against racist laws in South Africa.

hard.funny_explanation: It's like a big kid coming into your room, declaring your bed is now their 'colony,' and eating all your snacks while making you do their homework.

examples.text: Many African and Asian nations struggled for decades to end European colonialism.
My cat practices colonialism by occupying my laptop and refusing to leave until I pay a 'treat tax'.

hard.real_world_analogy: A neighbor moving into your garden, building a fence, and telling you that you can only grow the carrots they like.

words.meaning: Taking part in an activity or event.

medium.simple_explanation: Joining in and taking part in an activity or event.
medium.funny_explanation: Actually getting off the bleachers and playing the game instead of just shouting from the sidelines.

examples.text: Many women were participating in the protest marches for the first time.
I was participating in the dance-off until I realized I have two left feet.

words.meaning: Relating to citizens or people of a country.
Refusal to follow laws or commands.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Introduced in the context of the 'Civil Disobedience Movement' where people peacefully refused to follow British laws.
hard.simple_explanation: The act of refusing to obey rules or someone in authority.
hard.funny_explanation: When your mom says 'Clean your room' and you just sit there like a frozen statue—that's disobedience (though the 'Civil' part means doing it for a good cause and without being mean!).

examples.text: The students' civil disobedience forced the school to change its strict uniform policy.
The puppy showed total disobedience by eating the 'How to Train Your Dog' manual.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a silent protest where everyone in a cafeteria refuses to eat the mystery meat until the menu is improved.

words.meaning: Knowledge gained by doing or seeing things.

medium.simple_explanation: Knowledge or skill gained from doing, seeing, or feeling things.
medium.funny_explanation: The difference between reading a book about fire and accidentally touching a hot stove.

examples.text: The experience of joining the movement changed the lives of many people.
My only experience with cooking involves a microwave and a lot of luck.

words.meaning: Relating to government and how it works.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to the government, laws, and how a country is run.
medium.funny_explanation: The fancy world of suits, speeches, and people arguing about who gets to hold the big stick.

examples.text: The political leaders met to discuss the future of the nation.
Choosing a movie for family night turned into a huge political debate.

words.meaning: People who guide or head a group.
To be different or not the same.
In a very clear or strong way.

medium.simple_explanation: In a very clear, sudden, or strong way.
medium.funny_explanation: Like the difference between a dull pencil and one that could poke a hole through space-time.

examples.text: The leaders differed sharply on how the new laws should be written.
The temperature dropped sharply as soon as I forgot my jacket.

words.meaning: Keeping things apart or not together.
Groups of people who are allowed to vote.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Refers to the different groups of voters that leaders like Ambedkar and Gandhi disagreed over.
hard.simple_explanation: All the people in a country or area who are entitled to vote in an election.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'Electorate' is basically the VIP guest list for the giant party where we decide who gets to run the country.

examples.text: The political party tried to appeal to the rural electorates by promising better irrigation.
If the classroom electorate were in charge, we'd probably vote for 23 hours of recess and 1 hour of pizza.

hard.real_world_analogy: The student body of a school is the 'electorate' when it's time to choose a Head Boy or Head Girl.

words.meaning: Opposing the rule of another country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe movements in Kenya and India that were fighting against foreign rule.
hard.simple_explanation: Opposing or resisting the control of one country by another.
hard.funny_explanation: If colonialism is the uninvited guest who won't leave, anti-colonialism is the group of roommates standing together with 'Please Go Home' signs.

examples.text: The anti-colonial struggle in Kenya eventually led to its independence from Britain.
My anti-colonial movement against my brother taking over the top bunk is currently in a stalemate.

hard.real_world_analogy: A team of superheroes fighting back against an alien invasion that is trying to take over Earth's resources.

words.meaning: To look for similarities between two things.

medium.simple_explanation: To look at two or more things to see how they are the same.
medium.funny_explanation: Like checking if your lunch looks better than your friend's lunch.

examples.text: The teacher asked us to compare the independence movements of India and Kenya.
Don't compare my singing to a professional; compare it to a dying whale.

words.meaning: To show the differences between two things.

medium.simple_explanation: To look at two or more things to see how they are different.
medium.funny_explanation: Like seeing the difference between a peaceful kitten and a tornado with fur.

examples.text: The essay will contrast the different methods used by the leaders.
The neon green shoes really contrast with his all-black outfit.

words.meaning: Relating to a whole country or nation.
Free from outside control or rule.

medium.simple_explanation: Not being ruled or controlled by another person or country.
medium.funny_explanation: The glorious moment you finally get your own room and don't have to share your toys.

examples.text: India finally became an independent nation in 1947.
I want to be independent, but I still need my parents to pay for my pizza.

words.meaning: Short and using only a few words.
The process of increasing or developing.
Love and pride for one's own country.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Explains how the feeling of belonging to one nation helped Indians unite against the British.
hard.simple_explanation: A strong feeling of pride in and devotion to one's own country.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like being the world's biggest fan of your own country—wearing the jersey, singing the anthem, and wanting your 'team' to win independence.

examples.text: Nationalism grew in India as people from different backgrounds united for freedom.
My dog shows a weird kind of nationalism; he thinks our backyard is a sovereign country and barks at all 'invading' squirrels.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like the intense loyalty you feel for your school house during Sports Day.

words.meaning: Lands ruled by a powerful far country.

medium.simple_explanation: Countries or areas that are controlled by a more powerful country far away.
medium.funny_explanation: It's like someone else moving into your house, eating your food, and making all the rules.

examples.text: Britain had many colonies across Africa and Asia.
The ants established several colonies under the kitchen sink.

words.meaning: Connected or joined together.
Large global war from 1914 to 1918.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The book asks how this global conflict triggered economic and political changes in India.
hard.simple_explanation: A massive global war from 1914 to 1918 involving many of the world's powerful nations.
hard.funny_explanation: The ultimate 'everyone-fighting-everyone' rumble that changed the map of the world forever.

examples.text: The First World War led to a huge increase in defense expenditure for the British government in India.
History class without the First World War would be like a pizza without crust—missing a huge part of the base!

hard.real_world_analogy: A massive argument in a playground that starts between two kids but eventually sucks in every single student in the school.

words.meaning: Very angry about something unfair or bad.

medium.simple_explanation: Feeling very angry and shocked by something that is unfair or wrong.
medium.funny_explanation: That level of mad you get when you realize someone ate the leftovers you were thinking about all day.

examples.text: The people were outraged by the unfair laws passed by the government.
I was outraged when the vending machine took my money but gave me nothing.

words.meaning: Law that allowed arrest of political prisoners.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Introduced as a repressive law that allowed the British to arrest people without trial, sparking massive protests.
hard.simple_explanation: A 1919 British law in India that gave the government power to imprison people for two years without any trial.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a rule where a teacher could put you in detention for a month just because they *thought* you might whisper, and you weren't even allowed to explain yourself!

examples.text: The Rowlatt Act was called the 'Black Act' because it took away basic civil rights.
The Rowlatt Act was basically the British government saying 'I don't need a reason to ground you, I just feel like it!'

hard.real_world_analogy: A referee red-carding a player without them even committing a foul, and then refusing to let the VAR check the replay.

words.meaning: To take back or stop something.

medium.simple_explanation: To stop participating in something or to take something back.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you start to enter a cold pool, touch the water, and immediately pull your foot back.

examples.text: Gandhiji decided to withdraw the movement after it became violent.
I had to withdraw my hand from the cookie jar when I heard footsteps.

words.meaning: Protest based on truth and non-violence.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: This is Gandhi's core philosophy of non-violent resistance mentioned as a key question.
hard.simple_explanation: A method of non-violent resistance or 'truth-force' introduced by Mahatma Gandhi.
hard.funny_explanation: Defeating a bully not by fighting back, but by being so incredibly calm and honest that the bully eventually feels silly and stops.

examples.text: Gandhiji used satyagraha to fight against the unfair taxes in Champaran.
I tried a mini-satyagraha against eating broccoli, but my mom's 'dessert-force' was much stronger.

hard.real_world_analogy: Being so persistent and polite about a problem that the other person eventually has to listen to the truth of your situation.

words.meaning: Printed paper with news and events.
A written description of an event.

medium.simple_explanation: A written or spoken description of something that has happened.
medium.funny_explanation: Basically a 'What I Did Over Summer Vacation' but for serious grown-up stuff like wars and laws.

examples.text: The journalist had to write a report on the protest for the newspaper.
The weather report promised sun, but it rained cats and dogs.

words.meaning: Place where a famous violent event happened.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The site of one of the most tragic events in Indian history, where General Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful crowd.
hard.simple_explanation: A public garden in Amritsar where a horrific massacre took place on April 13, 1919.
hard.funny_explanation: A name every Indian student knows; it sounds like a quiet park, but it represents the loudest moment of the struggle for freedom.

examples.text: The Jallianwala Bagh incident turned the Indian people completely against British rule.
The story of Jallianwala Bagh is the part of history class where everyone stops joking and listens carefully.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a peaceful town square that suddenly becomes the center of a world-changing event.

words.meaning: The cruel killing of many people.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe the brutal and mass killing of people at Jallianwala Bagh.
hard.simple_explanation: The cruel and violent killing of a large number of people, especially those who cannot defend themselves.
hard.funny_explanation: It's a heavy word for a terrible event where things go way beyond a 'fight' into something much worse and one-sided.

examples.text: The world was shocked by the massacre of unarmed civilians in the park.
My high scores in the video game resulted in a total massacre of the alien invaders.

hard.real_world_analogy: A wolf entering a sheep pen where the sheep have no way to get out.

words.meaning: A group chosen for a special task.

medium.simple_explanation: An official group of people chosen to investigate or do a specific job.
medium.funny_explanation: A super-serious squad sent by the government to figure things out, usually with lots of clipboards.

examples.text: The Simon Commission was sent to India to look at the government system.
I formed a commission with my siblings to find out who stole the TV remote.

words.meaning: Pictures or statues of someone.
India shown as a mother goddess.

medium.simple_explanation: A symbolic image representing India as a mother goddess.
medium.funny_explanation: The ultimate Superhero Mom who represents an entire country instead of just one family.

examples.text: Artists created images of Bharat Mata to inspire people to love their country.
In old paintings, Bharat Mata looks way more organized than my actual room.

words.meaning: A figure representing the German nation.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Given as a comparative example to 'Bharat Mata,' showing how different nations used female figures to represent the country.
hard.simple_explanation: The female personification of the German nation.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of her as the 'Wonder Woman' of Germany—a powerful lady with a crown of oak leaves representing strength and peace.

examples.text: Artists painted Germania holding a sword and a shield to inspire German unity.
If Germania were alive today, she'd probably have a lot of followers on Instagram for her cool oak-leaf crown.

hard.real_world_analogy: Just like 'Bharat Mata' represents the spirit of India, 'Germania' represents the spirit of Germany.
